summary: When someone tells Nora she has something wrong, she now notices — on that same turn.
details: If a message mentions something she is currently holding a claim about, that claim is put in front of a small dedicated check that asks one question: is this person contradicting it, or just talking about it? Almost always just talking, and that answer costs nothing.

The check exists because a word list cannot tell 'no, big walk is a video game' from 'no I can't make the big walk'. The first contradicts a claim and the second declines an invitation, and they look identical to any rule made of words.

Which claims are even considered is decided without a model, from what she actually rendered and what the message actually says — so a model can never reach a claim nobody put in front of it, and can never name one by its internal id.
A contradiction reaches both what she knows and what she thinks a word means, since a person correcting a term is correcting both.
If the check cannot be reached, a deliberately narrow fallback still catches the clearest case: a reply to something she said, naming the thing, with a plain negation.
If nothing is running that could resolve disputes, she declines to mark rather than piling up corrections nothing will ever clear.
limitations: Only messages addressed to her are examined. A correction said to the room and not to her is not seen, which is a deliberate limit on cost rather than an oversight.

Related claims are matched by wording rather than by knowing two names mean one thing, so a correction phrased differently from the stored claim may not reach it. That improves when subjects gain identities.
